iterations.label: Front — blank frame template (border + empty banner + logo)
iterations.prompt:
Render as a clean, modern, FLAT comic illustration in the style of the "At His Command" reference art: bold, sharp, high-contrast, and completely smooth. This is a crisp DIGITAL vector-style illustration — NOT a photograph, and NOT a textured, printed, or vintage page.

Rendering: every shape is filled with ONE perfectly smooth, uniform, solid flat color, like a flat vector fill. There is ABSOLUTELY NO surface texture anywhere in the image: no grain, no noise, no speckle, no dithering, no paper/canvas/newsprint/parchment look — including on the borders and background. Bold, confident, SHARP black ink outlines with varied weight. NO gradients, NO blends, NO airbrush, NO halftone or Ben-Day dots.

Color palette: warm-dominant orange-and-blue complementary palette — golden amber #F9C233 as the primary background field, deep navy #16223C as the border/frame color, cream #FBE5A0 for the bottom banner strip and the logo badge, burnt orange #C96A10 and signal red #CC1616 as small accents within the logo only, ink black #101010 for linework.

THIS IS A BLANK TEMPLATE — an empty postcard front with NO scene, NO people, NO robots, NO monitors, NO objects, NO illustration of any kind in the main field. The main interior area is simply a plain, perfectly flat, empty golden amber (#F9C233) field with no content on it whatsoever — completely empty, just flat color, like a blank canvas waiting for future artwork.

The ONLY things rendered on this card, all sitting on top of that plain empty field:
1. A deep navy comic-style border frame (solid flat navy, no texture) running along all four outer edges of the card, matching a bold hand-inked comic panel border.
2. A single cream-colored banner strip running the FULL WIDTH across the very bottom edge, edge to edge — completely EMPTY, with absolutely NO text, letters, or marks of any kind inside it. Just a flat empty cream rectangle.
3. In the bottom-right corner, sitting directly on the amber field just above the empty cream banner (no dark box behind it): the League logo badge — "THE LEAGUE OF AMAZING PROGRAMMERS" stacked wordmark in a small cream rounded panel with a black keyline: "THE LEAGUE OF" small, "AMAZING" huge bold orange condensed caps, small lightning bolts, bar-lines over "OF", "PROGRAMMERS" below.

TEXT — the ONLY lettering anywhere on this card is the League logo badge described above, spelled exactly as given. The bottom banner must be completely blank — no lettering of any kind in it. No other lettering, signs, labels, or captions anywhere.

PRINT BLEED — this card is printed with a 1/8in bleed trimmed away after cutting, so a hair of overscan on any side is safe and expected. Only the navy border may run to and past the very edge — that's just border being trimmed off. The empty cream banner and the League logo must stay clearly inboard, with a generous margin of navy or amber visible around them, never touching or crossing the frame edge.

Follow the attached reference image closely for the exact border thickness, banner proportions, logo design, and color values — this is meant to be the same visual frame, just with the scene content and banner text removed.
iterations.negative_prompt: Any people, kids, students, figures, robots, monitors, desks, keyboards, furniture, or any illustrated scene or object of any kind in the main field. Any text, lettering, numbers, or symbols in the bottom banner — it must be completely empty and flat. Any lettering anywhere except the League logo badge. Texture, grain, speckle, parchment, aged-paper, halftone, Ben-Day dots, gradients, or blends. More than the specified colors. Blurry or muddy rendering. Portrait/vertical orientation. A black or dark box behind the League logo. Photorealism, 3D render, CGI. The logo, banner, or border touching or crossing the frame edge (other than the border's own bleed).
iterations.notes: Derived from Engineers-Anywhere-Postcard iter-005 with scene/text removed — border, empty banner, and logo only. Banner text will be an HTML overlay region, not baked into the image.
